title: Canopticon record — the model every page renders from
description: One document in; one read; sixteen kinds of derivation, each a verbatim span or dropped; three filing axes; links, never pages. Written to be built against. Every property a page shows is here; nothing a page shows is computed at render.

Piece.description: A document. Whole, never edited. Published at upload. One row in `pieces`.

slug.description: Permanent. A new version keeps it.

title.description: The headline. From the first H1 with any series marker removed by SERIES_MARKER (a regex, no model), tested against 16 real titles: /^(?:<project>[,:]?\s*)?(?:(?:Fourth|Fifth|Sixth|Seventh|Eighth|Ninth|Tenth|\w+teenth|\d+(?:st|nd|rd|th)?)\s+)?(?:Research\s+)?Pass(?:\s+(?:Six|Seven|Eight|Nine|Ten|\d+))?[:\s—-]+|\s*[—:-]\s*(?:A\s+)?(?:\w+\s+)?(?:Research\s+)?Pass(?:\s+for\s+<project>)?\s*$|\s*\((?:Research\s+)?Pass\s*\d+[^)]*\)/i. The project name is stripped only when it is the prefix that filed the piece. No match → unchanged. The slug is made from this. The read may also replace a filename-shaped title with a verbatim line. The original is always kept in title_original and emitted as alternativeHeadline.

sequence.description: The number the series marker carried, if any. Order within a project, never identity: ties and gaps sort by published_at. Default parent_piece_id is the previous sequence in the project, until the operator sets lineage explicitly. Emitted as CreativeWorkSeries.position.

series_marker.description: The exact text removed, e.g. 'Ancaster Pass 18:', '— Eighth Research Pass for Ancaster', '(Research Pass 19, September 2026)'. Shown on the bench with Revert.

dek.description: The document's own italic line or first sentence. Never written for it.

status.description: The three words. `published` = live, not yet read. `read` = derivations exist. `failed` = one sentence in failure_reason and a Retry.

visibility.description: public = everything served (upload is publication). held = a personal document, nothing served (404). evidence_only = derived blocks served, body and case sections absent, a labelled bar per held section. Chosen on the desk; the read proposes held for any document about its author.

section_roles.description: One per section, for personal documents. case = the subject is the author rather than the literature. Derivations anchored only in a case section are desk-only.

failure_reason.description: The exact string the read wrote. e.g. 'PDF has no text layer — nothing was read.'

source_id.description: The stored text this piece is rendered from and verified against.

project_id.description: Axis 1. Zero or one. Read from a title prefix ('Ancaster Pass 16 …', 'ALDERSHOT —'), confirmed by the operator. Most pieces are null: standalone.

topic_ids.description: Axis 3. Zero or more. Every topic appears on public pages; status=undone topics are removed and never named again.

parent_piece_id.description: Lineage: grew from. Set at upload or at publish. Never inferred.

read_at.description: Also the sitemap lastmod. Never fabricated.

Kind.description: Axis 2. Read from the file's shape and its own word for itself; operator can change it. A closed list — add to it deliberately.

Origin.description: How the document arrived. Kept beside it forever; shown as 'Arrived as' in the rail.

url.description: For method=url: the pasted link, e.g. a claude.ai/public/artifacts/… page. Fetched at the edge; JS pages rendered by Browser Rendering; stored as Markdown. Emitted in JSON-LD as isBasedOn when the link is not the author's own.

sha256.description: Of the stored bytes. An identical file is refused before anything is written.

Source.description: The extracted text a piece is verified against. First 8 KB inline, the rest in R2.

ReadReceipt.description: What the read did. Shown as the strip under every title; nothing is hidden, including drops.

chars_read.description: Equal to source.char_count — 'Read in full'. If a document ever exceeds one call, the read is split by section and this still equals the total; there is no partial read.

spans_dropped.description: Proposed spans that were not a literal substring of the source. Always shown.

shape_blocks.description: How many blocks came from the file's own shape (no model): TL;DR, Key Findings, Decisions, Kill criteria, Caveats, Sources.

Quote.description: A verbatim span. The primitive everything else points at. One receipt page (/q/<id>) each.

text.description: Exactly as in source.content_text[start:end]. Re-located by code at every render; if it no longer matches, the item is hidden and counted, never shown wrong.

section.description: The § label shown inline: '§2', 'TL;DR', 'KF3'. From the nearest heading above start.

anchor.description: Content-addressed: 'q-' + first 6 hex of sha256(text). Survives re-reads and new versions as long as the words do. This is the citable fragment: /p/<slug>#q-8a3f2c.

Derivation.description: One thing the read found. Every derivation has exactly one quote it is anchored to, or it does not exist. The machine never adds a judgment: `standing`, `source_type` and `verb` are the document's own words.

origin.description: shape = from the file's structure, no model (TL;DR, headings, numbered Key Findings, 'Decision N', 'Kill criteria', 'Caveats', '## Sources', [n] markers). read = from the one model call.

order.description: Document order. Pages never reorder within a kind.

label.description: The short form shown in a table cell or a list.

figure.description: kind=figure. The number as written: '83.2%', 'HR 4.56', 'n = 814,689', '48–72 h'.

measures.description: kind=figure. What it measures, in the document's words.

period.description: kind=figure|event. The date or range as written.

attributed_to.description: kind=figure|claim. Who reported or said it, as written.

source_type.description: kind=figure. The document's OWN rating of the source, verbatim or near: 'independent', 'vendor', 'vendor claim', 'rule', 'regulator', 'third-party review', 'assumption', 'the document's own design'. null when the document gives none. Never assigned by the machine.

rejected.description: kind=figure. True when the document itself says not to rely on it ('Do not cite them', 'treat as marketing'). Rendered struck through, kept so nothing lifts it as fact.

standing.description: kind=claim. The document's own word for what the claim is: 'independent evidence', 'vendor claim', 'rule', 'interpretation', 'assumption', 'invention — to validate', 'clinical — flagged'. Replaces the old pro/critical/neutral stance.

direction.description: kind=evidence. As the document frames it. Between this document's own facts and claims only — never across documents.

target_derivation_id.description: kind=evidence. The claim it bears on.

answer_quote_id.description: kind=question. The sentence that answers, verbatim. The question is rendered as a heading, the answer as its first sentence — page structure, not FAQ markup.

resolves_when.description: kind=prediction. Shown only on the document, project and topic pages, in context, never as a bare list on the desk or front. The document's own condition, when stated: 'the 90-day read-out', 'a published study'.

resolved_by_piece_id.description: kind=prediction. Set by the operator when a later document answers it; the two pages then link. No score.

starred.description: kind=recommendation. The document's own ★ / RECOMMENDED marker.

verb.description: kind=relation. The verb as the document wrote it — 'shut down by', 'requires', 'authored', 'credits'. Not a taxonomy.

is_thesis_proposed.description: kind=thesis. The sentence where the document states its own central claim or names its contribution as novel ('the genuine wedge', 'should stop being … and become …', 'Novel theoretical contribution'). Verbatim. Shown on Essays as a proposed thesis; the operator may also type a thesis of their own. Dismissed → Ignore.

outbound_url.description: kind=source. Resolved from a URL in the text, a DOI, or a [n] entry. Every resolvable source is an outbound link and a JSON-LD `citation`. null = listed as written, linked to nothing.

citation_marker.description: kind=source. The document's own [n]. In-body markers link to #s-<n>; the sources list is numbered as the document numbers it.

role.description: What kind of statement the anchoring passage is. finding = a fact about the world with a source; reasoning = the document's own inference; recommendation = advice to the author; premise = the author's own decision or assumption echoed back ("given that you send the newsletter yourself…"). Articles may quote only finding and reasoning as evidence; recommendation and premise may be mentioned, labelled as such, never used to support a claim. Set at read time; editable on the desk.

Project.description: Axis 1: something the operator is making, with a sequence of its own. Not a subject. Ancaster, Aldershot, Canopticon. A hub page only once its note is written.

title_prefixes.description: Patterns that file a new upload here automatically: 'Ancaster Pass', 'Ancaster,', 'ALDERSHOT', 'Aldershot:'. Operator-edited.

note_md.description: Written by the operator. Its existence is what makes /c/<slug> indexable; without it the hub is noindex.

Topic.description: Axis 3: what documents are about. Named by the read from recurring terms and applied at once; rename or undo on the desk; crosses projects. Never created by the machine alone.

name.description: Named by the read from the top term; the operator may rename it on the desk.

status.description: live: filed and shown on every public page the moment the read names it. undone: removed by the operator; never named again.

term_labels.description: The evidence: the terms behind the topic, matched by lower(label). Edit the list and the topic follows.

named_because.description: Shown on the bench: 'FINTRAC, RPAA, GST/HST, 1099-K and merchant of record appear in 4 Ancaster documents and nowhere else.'

note_md.description: Same rule as projects: the note makes the page.

Reading.description: The operator's note on a passage. The human half of verification. Public, in the margin.

Ignore.description: Anything the operator dismissed from the bench. It never returns.

Protocol.description: A test the document asks its reader to run. One per document at most; every field is a verbatim span. A protocol with no measure is a recommendation. See HANDOFF.md → Protocol.

duration_days.description: Parsed from the text ('two weeks' → 14); null when the document gives none.

kill_quote_id.description: Set when the document states a stop condition ('less than 10 percentage points above baseline').

Tracker.description: Desk-only. A protocol the operator started. Nothing here is served publicly; a completed or stopped tracker may be written up as a piece of kind 'result' that grew from the proposing document.

Draft.description: An essay in progress. One row per draft; sections stream in. See HANDOFF.md → The essay engine.

thesis_quote_id.description: Set when the thesis is a document's own sentence.

Pitch.description: NOT a table. Five queries, each producing a candidate issue for the Letter with a verbatim hook. No model. Dismissed pitches go to Ignore.

Link.description: NOT a table. A query, shown here as the shape the renderer consumes. Shared term → link both ways at the passage. Named source → link outward. Lineage → grew from / into. Same measure → figures grouped by lower(measures) across pieces, never reconciled.

to.description: A piece id + quote anchor, or an outbound URL.

MachineTwins.description: What exists beside every page, and its indexing rule. All emitted from this model; none computed at render by a model.

/p/<slug>.const: HTML. Indexed. JSON-LD: Article (headline, datePublished, dateModified=read_at, author Person with sameAs, isPartOf CreativeWorkSeries=project when project_id, isBasedOn=parent or origin.url, citation[]=sources with outbound_url, mentions[]=DefinedTerm per topic and per term, hasPart[]=Quotation for readings, license). No FAQPage markup — question/answer is page structure.

/p/<slug>.md.const: Byte-exact body with front matter. X-Robots-Tag: noindex. Link: <page>; rel=canonical.

/p/<slug>.json.const: This model for one piece. noindex.

/c/<project>.const: Hub. Indexed only when project.note_md exists; else noindex.

/t/<topic>.const: Hub. Indexed only when note_md exists; else noindex.

/essays/<slug>.const: An essay. Person-written; indexed; cites record pages and the outside sources they name (citation[]); parent_piece_id = the pitch's document; optionally sent by email via Resend when the key is set.

/search.const: FTS5 over quotes and pieces. Always noindex.

/llms.txt.const: One line per indexed page, grouped by project then topic, using dek or first sentence. Fetches counted, not assumed.

/sitemap.xml.const: Indexed pages only, lastmod = read_at or published_at. IndexNow ping on publish and new version.

Rules.description: The invariants. A build that violates one is wrong.
const: Upload is publication. A new version keeps the slug and the origin.
The headline is the author's title with any series marker removed by a rule; the original is kept and shown; the number is order, not a name; the body is never edited.
Each document is read once, whole, in one call. Three statuses. No chunks, no passes, no tab-open poller.
Every derivation has one quote; the quote is a literal substring of the source, re-checked at render. Dropped counts are always shown.
The machine adds no judgment: standing, source_type, verb, rejected and starred are the document's own words. Nothing is graded, reconciled or summarised across documents.
The machine makes links; only a person makes pages. Hubs are indexed only with a written note. Filters, search, receipts and twins are noindex.

Nothing publishes until the operator approves or edits it; the page records how it was made (drafted with Claude and approved, or written by the operator). A draft arrives whole — quotes verified, outside sources linked, counter-evidence and the settling test as sections, unreceipted sentences dotted — and is labelled as Claude's until then.
No model runs at render time, anywhere.
The record never edits the author's prose to please an engine. Structure and receipts are added around the text; the text is never touched.
AI crawlers are allowed at the edge and the allowance is checked weekly; fetches, referrals and queries are shown on the bench per document.
Anything the operator ignores never returns.
